q: 1. The first stage of a large construction work to ............
explain: The life cycle of any project begins with the 'Conception' phase, where the basic idea or need for the project is identified before any feasibility studies or designs begin.

q: 2. A construction team includes ............
explain: A standard construction team is a multidisciplinary group comprising the owner (client), the lead designers (architects/engineers), and the contractors.

q: 3. The conception of idea for any construction work is ............
explain: The owner (client) is the one who perceives the need for a project and initiates the conception of the idea.

q: 4. The field of activities of an engineer includes ............
options: approval of construction plans by the local authority
inspection and payment of work done by contractor
explain: Engineers are responsible for the technical lifecycle, including quantity surveying (estimation), regulatory compliance (approvals), and project management (inspection/valuation).

q: 5. The earnest money deposited by unsuccessful bidder is returned after ............
explain: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) acts as a guarantee that the bidder will enter the contract. Once the contract is officially awarded to the winner, the money is returned to the unsuccessful parties.

q: 6. The number of members in dispute resolution board is ............
explain: A Dispute Resolution Board (DRB) typically consists of either a single member (one-person board) or three members, depending on the contract's scale and complexity.

q: 7. Which of the following is the ultimate method of dispute resolution in any contract ............
explain: While arbitration and DRBs are common, 'Litigation' in a court of law is the final legal recourse if all alternative dispute resolution (ADR) methods fail.

q: 8. The total cost versus time curve is ............
explain: The total cost curve is U-shaped because it is the sum of direct costs (which decrease with more time) and indirect costs (which increase over time).

q: 9. Crashing to the project means ............
options: reducing the time of completion by spending more resources
reducing the cost of project by delaying the time of completion
reducing the project size to save the resources
explain: Project crashing is the technique of adding extra resources (labor, overtime, equipment) to shorten the duration of critical activities.

q: 10. A hand-held air-operated percussion type drill used for drilling down holes is ............
explain: A jack hammer is a portable, hand-held pneumatic tool used primarily for vertical or down-hole drilling in rock or concrete.

q: 11. A drill most suitable for drilling down, horizontal, or up holes is ............
explain: A drifter is a heavy-duty rock drill mounted on a support (like a jumbo or frame) that can efficiently drill in various orientations: up, down, or horizontal.

q: 12. The bid review committee consists of ............ members of persons.
explain: In many public procurement frameworks, a three-member committee is standardized to ensure fairness and collective decision-making during bid evaluation.

q: 13. The penalty provision in any contract agreement is ............
explain: Liquidated damages or penalties for delay are commonly set at 0.05% of the contract price per day, often capped at 10% of the total value.

q: 14. When the time of earliest finish and the latest finish are equal in an operation, the operation is called ............
explain: If EF = LF, the total float is zero. Activities with zero float are termed 'Critical' because any delay in them will delay the entire project.

q: 15. The system of organization introduced by F.W. Taylor is known as ............
explain: F.W. Taylor, the father of Scientific Management, introduced the 'Functional Organization' system where specialists supervise specific functions across the board.

q: 16. A drawback of the bar chart is that ............
options: all the activity are independent of each other
it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
the sequence of activity is not clearly defined
explain: Gantt charts (bar charts) lack interdependency details, don't easily show the critical path, and can make it difficult to monitor precise progress in complex projects.

q: 17. Select the incorrect statement ............
options: a critical path always begins at the very first event
a critical path always terminates at the last event
critical activities control the project duration
critical activity is the one for which free float is zero
explain: While a critical activity has a Total Float of zero, having a Free Float of zero is not the defining characteristic, as non-critical activities can also have zero free float.

q: 18. Select the incorrect statements ............
options: its latest start time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest starts time
its latest finish time and earliest starts time for its successor activity
its earliest finish time and latest time for its successor activity
explain: The latest start time of an activity is not directly equated to the earliest start time of its successor; these values depend on activity duration and float.

q: 19. Free float is the ............
explain: Free float is the portion of total float that can be used without affecting the early start of the immediately following successor activity.

q: 20. Critical path is ............
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the first event to the last event
ideal path by preceding along which the project can be completed as per the schedule
the path which takes into account the completion of all the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is the specific sequence of activities that represents the minimum time required to complete the project as scheduled.

q: 21. Resource smoothening means ............
options: adjustment of resources to have the least variations
complete revamping of resources to suit the requirement
optimisation and economical utilisation of resources
explain: Resource smoothing is a technique used to level the peaks and valleys of resource demand within the limits of the project's float.

q: 22. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to critical path is known as ............
explain: A 'Semi-critical' or 'Sub-critical' path is a path that has a very low amount of float and can easily become a critical path if minor delays occur.

q: 23. Which of the following is a dummy activity?
options: Await the arrival of concrete material
explain: A dummy activity is one that consumes no time or resources but represents a logical dependency. 'Awaiting arrival' is a common example of an artificial delay/dependency.

q: 24. The time by which the completion of an activity can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities is called ............
explain: Free Float is the amount of time that an activity can be delayed without delaying the Earliest Start (ES) of any successor.

q: 25. Fulkerson's rule is used for numbering the ............
explain: Fulkerson's Rule provides a systematic procedure for numbering events (nodes) in a project network diagram in a logical order.

q: 26. The minimum number of consulting firms for direct purchase of service is ............
explain: In competitive procurement environments, usually at least 3 firms are required to ensure a fair price comparison for service acquisition.

q: 27. Quality control during construction consists largely of ensuring ............
explain: The core of Quality Control (QC) is ensuring 'conformance'—verifying that the work performed meets the pre-defined standards, specifications, and requirements.

q: 28. The department head can extend the time upto ............% of initial contract duration.
explain: Administrative rules often limit the authority of a department head to approve time extensions to 25% of the original duration; beyond this, higher approval is usually required.

q: 29. Sand is produced by crushing in ............
explain: A ball mill is a type of grinder used for grinding and blending materials into very fine particles, including producing manufactured sand.

q: 30. Trenching machines cannot be used for ............
explain: Standard trenching machines are designed for soil and clay; they are generally unable to cut through solid rock formations without specialized rock-saw attachments.

q: 31. The probability distribution taken to represent the completion time in P.E.R.T. analysis is ............
explain: PERT assumes that the duration of an activity follows a Beta Distribution, which accounts for the asymmetry between optimistic and pessimistic times.

q: 32. According to Beta distribution, the standard deviation of the time of completion is given by ............
explain: Standard deviation ($σ$) in PERT is calculated as $(t_p - t_o) / 6$, where $t_p$ is pessimistic time and $t_o$ is optimistic time.

q: 33. The optimistic, most likely and pessimistic time estimates of an activity are 5, 10, 21 days, what are the expected time and standard deviation?
explain: Expected time $T_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p)/6 = (5 + 40 + 21)/6 = 11$. Standard deviation $σ = (21-5)/6 = 2.67$.

q: 34. A golden rule for the procurement of construction stores is that ............
options: half of the construction stores should be at work site and half under procurement
two-third of the construction stores should be at work site and one-third under procurement
three-fourth of the construction stores should be at work site and one-fourth under procurement
whole of the construction store should be at work site
explain: Effective inventory management often uses the 'Two-Thirds Rule' to balance availability at the site with material currently in the supply chain.

q: 35. The construction works costing below rupees twenty thousand are classified as ............
explain: Small-scale works with low financial thresholds (like Rs. 20,000) are typically categorized as 'Minor Works' for administrative and accounting purposes.

q: 36. The construction costing above rupees one lac are classified as ............
explain: Works exceeding a certain financial threshold (often Rs. 100,000 or 1 Lac) are typically classified as 'Projects' requiring detailed planning and approval.

q: 37. The project technical audit is done ............
explain: A technical audit is primarily conducted once the project is physically complete to verify that all technical specifications were followed and quality standards were met.

q: 38. Weight-batching proceeds on ............
options: the assumption of the declared weight in each bag of cement
weighing the contents of each bag
accurately estimating the weight of each material to be used in each batch
the assumption of correct dry weight of each size range of each material and the weight of water
explain: Weight-batching involves measuring all concrete constituents by weight to ensure the most accurate mix proportioning and consistency.

q: 39. Cost-benefit studies are essential to ............
options: assess the total cost of the work
ascertain the relevant escalation in prices
evaluate the viability and worthwhileness of taking up the project
explain: A Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) is a financial assessment tool used to determine if the benefits of a project outweigh the costs before starting.

q: 40. Grader is used mainly for ............
explain: A motor grader is primarily used for fine grading, leveling, shaping, and finishing the surface of the road base or sub-grade.

q: 41. In P.E.R.T. technique, completion of an activity is called ............
explain: In network diagrams, the node at the end of an activity represents its completion and is called the 'Head Event'.

q: 42. Higher standard deviations means ............
explain: In statistics and PERT, a higher standard deviation indicates a wider range of possible outcomes, which directly corresponds to higher risk and uncertainty.

q: 43. Slack is given as the difference between ............
options: latest allowable time and earliest expected time
latest allowable time and the pessimistic time estimate
earliest expected time and latest allowable time
final event time and initial event time
explain: Event Slack = Latest Allowable Time ($T_L$) - Earliest Expected Time ($T_E$).

q: 44. Negative slack indicates ............
explain: Negative slack occurs when the time required to complete the project ($T_E$) exceeds the time available ($T_L$), indicating the project is behind schedule.

q: 45. For all the events along the critical path, the slack is ............
explain: By definition, events on the critical path have the least amount of flexibility, meaning their slack is zero (or the minimum constant value in the network).

q: 46. A dummy activity in a network ............
options: is represented by a dotted line
does not consume time or resources
explain: Dummies are artificial activities shown with dashed arrows to represent logical dependencies without adding time or cost to the project.

q: 47. In the critical path of construction planning, free float can be ............
explain: Free float is a subset of Total Float, and mathematically, Free Float is always greater than or equal to Independent Float ($TF ≥ FF ≥ IF$).

q: 48. Which of the following is a dummy activity?
options: awaiting the arrivals of concrete material
explain: Wait times or administrative dependencies that don't involve active labor or machine work are modeled as dummies to maintain network logic.

q: 49. The construction of residential building are treated as ............
explain: Residential buildings involve standard materials and methods, typically categorized under 'Light Construction' compared to dams or industrial plants.

q: 50. The construction of ............ belongs to industrial construction.
explain: Industrial construction refers to highly specialized structures for manufacturing and processing, such as oil refineries and chemical plants.

q: 51. The construction of airport are treated as ............
explain: Airports involve large-scale earthwork, specialized paving for runways, and complex infrastructure, categorizing them as Heavy Construction.

q: 52. The pump suitable for high discharge pressure ............
explain: Reciprocating pumps are positive displacement pumps ideal for applications requiring high pressure at relatively low flow rates.

q: 53. Screw pumps are used for pumping ............
explain: Screw pumps handle high-viscosity fluids (like oil or sludge) efficiently because they move liquid axially without high turbulence.

q: 54. Which information has least hearing on the selection of the pump?
options: nature of liquid to be handled
explain: While the 'use' (purpose) is helpful context, technical selection is strictly governed by physical parameters like flow (capacity), fluid properties, and head (lift).

q: 55. The Contractor is responsible for ............
options: procuring material which is not supplied by the owner
organising and planning the work as per drawing
executing the work as per specifications laid down on the contact
explain: A contractor's primary role is the end-to-end execution, resource management, and compliance with the technical drawings and specs provided.

q: 56. The resources in a construction project are made up of ............
options: plant equipment and machinery required for the project
construction material such as cement, bricks, steel etc
explain: The 4 M's of construction resources are Men (Manpower), Materials, Machinery (Plant), and Money.

q: 57. The pre-tender stage of construction requires ............
explain: Before a tender is invited, the owner must ensure the land is available, the site is chosen, and the technical scope (design) is finalized.

q: 58. Technical planning is carried out for the ............
explain: Technical planning bridges the gap between the concept and execution by producing the precise drawings and cost calculations (estimates) needed.

q: 59. The post tender stage of construction consists of ............
explain: The post-tender phase covers everything from contract award through execution monitoring to the final settlement of accounts.

q: 60. For the preparation of a construction schedule, the data required is ............
explain: To build a schedule, you must know what needs to be done (activities), how they are grouped (operations), and how fast they can be done (labor productivity).

q: 61. When quarry rock is to be hauled, the body of a rear dump truck should be ............
options: deep with vertical or sloping side boards
explain: Deep bodies with reinforced sides are necessary to handle the impact and volume of heavy, abrasive quarry rocks.

q: 62. Bottom dump wagons are not suitable for ............
explain: Wet clay is sticky and cohesive; it tends to bridge or get stuck in the discharge gates of a bottom dump wagon.

q: 63. For three-dimensional movement of a weight, which one of the following is most suitable?
explain: Cranes provide 3D movement: vertical (hoisting), horizontal (trolleying/jib), and circular (slewing).

q: 64. The most suitable equipment for excavating trenches when the sides are permitted to establish their angles of repose, without shoring is ............
explain: A back-hoe (or hoe) is the standard for trenching because it digs below its own track level and provides excellent control for trench walls.

q: 65. Variance is ............
options: sum of time duration for various job / number of jobs
difference between number under consideration and mean time
mean of square root of mean of squared deviation
square root of mean of squared deviations
explain: In the context of PERT, variance ($σ^2$) is the square of the standard deviation, representing the mean of the squared deviations from the expected time.

q: 66. If for a activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is ............
67. Standard deviation when optimistic time and earliest expected time ............
explain: Standard Deviation $σ = (t_p - t_o) / 6$. For the values in Q66: $(8 - 1) / 6 = 1.167$.

options: difference of lastest allowable time and earliest expected time
earliest expected time - lastest allowable time
explain: Slack specifically refers to events (nodes) and is calculated as $T_L - T_E$.

q: 69. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: in a network activities are represented by arrows and events are circled
events into which a number of activities enter and from which one or several activities emerge are called the merge nodes
events into which one or several activities enter and from which a number of emerging activities are generated are called burst nodes
explain: These are the fundamental definitions of network components (arrows/nodes) and node types (merge/burst).

q: 70. Interfering float is the difference between ............
explain: Interfering Float ($IF = TF - FF$) is equal to the head event slack.

q: 71. Negative float for any activity means that the activity is ............
explain: An activity with negative float is 'Super-critical' because it is already behind the required completion date.

q: 72. Zero float any activity means that the activity is ............
explain: Zero float indicates a 'Critical' activity; any delay will immediately impact the project finish date.

q: 73. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is ............
explain: Positive float indicates a 'Sub-critical' or non-critical activity with some flexibility in its timing.

q: 74. The total float for any activity along the critical path in C.P.M. is ............
explain: The critical path is defined as the sequence of activities with zero total float.

q: 75. Direct cost a project is due to ............
options: establishment charges as salaries to administrative staff
cost of materials and wages of labour
explain: Direct costs are expenses directly attributable to a specific work item, such as labor wages and material costs.

q: 76. Total project cost ............
options: establishment charges as salaries to administrative staff
cost of materials and wages of labour
explain: Note: This question in the text appears to repeat the concept of direct cost. The answer 'd' refers to the core direct components.

q: 77. Total project cost ............
options: initially reduces and then increases with increase in time
initially increases and then reduces with increase in time
explain: Total cost follows a U-curve: as time increases, direct costs drop but indirect costs rise, leading to a minimum point.

q: 78. Total cost is ............
explain: The total project cost is the summation of Direct Costs and Indirect Costs (including overheads and contingency).

q: 79. Identify the odd man out ............
explain: 'Design completed' is an Event (a point in time), whereas the others are Activities (actions that consume time).

q: 80. An important principle in drawing a network is ............
options: no activity can start until all the previous activities in the same chain are completed
parallel activities should begin and end at the same time
between two events there should not be more than two activities
the number of dummy activities in a network should not exceed 4
explain: This is the principle of logical precedence; a successor cannot begin until its predecessors are finished.

q: 81. A dummy activity ............
options: has no tail event but only a head event
has only head event but tail event
does not require any resources or any time
has no bearing on the network and can appear anywhere
explain: Dummies are logical connectors only; they are 'zero-time' and 'zero-resource' activities.

q: 82. At an event other than final event if no activity emerges, it results in an error called ............
explain: Dangling occurs when an activity is not connected to the final event, leaving a 'loose end' in the middle of the network.

q: 83. Negative slack occurs ............
options: when lastest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events sticks to their schedule
explain: Negative slack indicates the project is behind schedule, often caused by inadequate resources or delays.

q: 84. Critical path ............
explain: The critical path is the longest sequence of activities, which means it has the least (minimum) amount of slack/float.

options: the earliest time by which an activity may commence
lastest time by which an activity can be delayed without hapering the completion of the project
lastest allowable time - earliest expected time
time available time required for an activity
explain: Float is the difference between the time available for an activity and the time required ($T_L - T_E$).

q: 86. Crashing is ............
explain: Crashing is the process of compressing the project schedule by shortening the duration of critical activities.

q: 87. Latest starts of an activity is always ............
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: The Latest Start ($LS$) must occur at or after the latest possible completion of the previous activity to maintain logic.

q: 88. 'Wait' in P.E.R.T., belongs to the category of ............
explain: Even though 'waiting' involves no physical work, it consumes time and is therefore treated as an activity.

q: 89. An activity of the project is graphically represented by ............ on the network
explain: In Activity-on-Arrow (AOA) diagrams, arrows represent tasks (activities).

q: 90. Which of the following statement is correct about the network diagram?
options: the events are represented graphically by circles or nodes at the beginning and the end of activity by arrows
the tail end of the arrow represents the start of the activity
the head of the arrow represents the end of an activity
explain: These are the standard conventions for drawing AOA (Activity-on-Arrow) network diagrams.

q: 91. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circle
explain: In a left-to-right flow network, activities on the left are predecessors and must be completed before those on the right.

q: 92. The chart which gives an estimate about the amount of materials handling between various workstation is known as ............
explain: A Travel Chart is a matrix used in layout planning to track the movement of materials or people between departments.

q: 93. Slack time in P.E.R.T. analysis ............
options: can never be greater than zero
is always zero for critical activities
can never be less than zero
explain: The critical path events are those with the minimum slack (usually zero, but can be negative if the project is behind).

q: 94. If the completion time for a particular project is 20 weeks and its earliest expected time is 22 weeks, then the slack time for the project is ............
explain: Slack = $T_L - T_E$. Here $20 - 22 = -2$ weeks.

q: 95. Interfering float is the difference between ............
explain: Interfering float is defined as $TF - FF$; it represents the part of the total float that, if used, consumes the slack of a successor event.

q: 96. Which of the following is not an excavating equipment?
explain: A Scraper is primarily an earth-moving (hauling and spreading) machine, whereas the others are dedicated excavators.

q: 97. For excavating solid rocks, the most suitable equipment?
explain: The power shovel provides the highest breakout force, making it the best choice for digging hard or blasted rock.

q: 98. The size of a power shovel is indicated by the size of ............
explain: Power shovels are rated by the capacity (volume) of their 'dipper' or bucket.

q: 99. Which one of the following does not from a part of Derrick crane?
explain: A Derrick crane consists of a mast, a boom (incorrectly spelled 'book' in text), and guy wires. A jack is a separate lifting tool.

q: 100. Which one of the following does not fall under the category hoisting equipment?
explain: A Dragline is excavating equipment. While it has hoisting cables, its primary function is excavation, not dedicated lifting like a hoist or jack.
